title: In a restaurant: order, ask, pay (Im Restaurant)
summary: Find a seat, order for two, ask about a dish, and pay: zusammen oder getrennt?
goals: Ask for a seat and the menu
Order for yourself and a friend
Ask for the bill, pay together or separately, and tip

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 3: In company (Eine Pizza bitte!, Zahlen bitte!)

sections.title: From the door to the bill
rows: Ein Bier und ein Wasser, bitte.

sections.title: Ordering for two
sections.text:
Order for a friend with [[für]] + the accusative from lesson 6:
- [[Für mich den Salat und für ihn den Fisch.]]
- [[Ich nehme die Suppe, und meine Freundin nimmt den Salat.]]
- [[Wir nehmen zwei Bier.]]

The waiter ([[der Kellner]], [[die Kellnerin]]) often asks the second person [[Und für Sie?]] (And for you?).

sections.title: Asking about a dish
sections.text:
- [[Was ist das?]] or [[Was ist ...?]] (Unit 2)
- [[Ist das scharf?]] = Is it spicy?
- [[Ist da Fleisch drin?]] = Is there meat in it? ([[drin]] = in it, a spoken chunk)
- [[Ich esse kein Fleisch.]] = I don't eat meat.
- [[Was empfehlen Sie?]] = What do you recommend? ([[empfehlen]] changes its vowel: [[du empfiehlst]], [[er empfiehlt]])

sections.title: Paying and tipping
sections.text:
For the bill: [[Zahlen, bitte!]] or [[Die Rechnung, bitte!]] The waiter usually comes to your table and asks [[Zusammen oder getrennt?]] (together or separately?). Splitting the bill is completely normal in Germany. Answer [[Zusammen, bitte.]] or [[Getrennt, bitte.]]

The waiter says the total: [[Das macht achtzehn Euro vierzig.]] Then you say the amount you want to pay, tip included: [[Zwanzig, bitte.]] Or you hand over the money and say [[Stimmt so.]] (keep the change). About 5-10% is normal; you know this from the Extras page.

sections.title: In a Munich beer garden
sections.text: Say [[Prost!]] when you clink glasses, and look the other person in the eye. In beer gardens and traditional places you often share a table with strangers: just ask [[Ist der Platz frei?]]

items.de: Guten Abend! Was möchten Sie trinken?
items.en: Good evening! What would you like to drink?

items.de: Ein Bier und ein Wasser, bitte.
items.en: A beer and a water, please.
And what would you like to eat?

items.de: Gut. Für mich die Suppe und für ihn den Fisch.
items.en: Good. The soup for me and the fish for him.

items.de: Zusammen, bitte. Ich lade dich ein, Eva!
items.en: Together, please. It's my treat, Eva!

items.question: You want the bill. What do you say?
items.explanation: Zahlen, bitte! or Die Rechnung, bitte! Guten Appetit = enjoy your meal, Prost = cheers.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: What do you recommend? (polite)
items.explanation: Sie empfehlen. The vowel changes only with du and er/sie/es: er empfiehlt.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: The salad for me and the fish for him.
items.text: Für mich den Salat und für ___ den Fisch.
items.explanation: für takes the accusative: er becomes ihn.

items.question: The waiter asks 'Zusammen oder getrennt?'. You and your friend each pay for yourselves. What do you say?
items.explanation: getrennt = separately: each pays for their own food.

items.question: How much is the bill?
items.explanation: achtzehn Euro vierzig = 18,40 €. Tip by saying a round number: Zwanzig, bitte.
